seo.title: zapzero · Inbox zero for WhatsApp
seo.description: Clear your WhatsApp. AI triages every chat and drafts replies in your own voice. No bot, no risk, never leaves your Mac.

sections.eyebrow: Mac app · local MCP for Claude
sections.title: Clear your WhatsApp.
sections.subtitle: Turn your WhatsApp Desktop into a local MCP for Claude, with a dedicated UX.
sections.body: Download the app and it reads your chats right there on your Mac, read-only. In the panel, AI shows who's waiting on you and leaves a reply written your way: Y opens WhatsApp with the text ready and you hit Enter. In Claude, one click connects zapzero and you ask "who's waiting on me?".
sections.installHint: Or copy the link and paste it into your agent (Claude Code, Codex…): it reads it and installs from the terminal:

steps.title: Reads your Mac. Only reads.
steps.text: zapzero opens WhatsApp Desktop's local database read-only. No extra linked device, no side API, and your chats go to no server of ours.

steps.title: AI triages everything.
steps.text: Who's waiting on whom, how urgent it is, who this person is to you. And for everyone waiting on you, a draft in your own voice. Your Claude does it, on your subscription.

steps.title: You clear it.
steps.text: Y opens the chat in WhatsApp with the reply typed in. You check it and hit Enter. Dates, prices, yes or no come as choices: pick one and the AI rewrites the whole sentence in your voice.

sections.title: Two apps you already have.

items.name: WhatsApp Desktop
items.text: The official Mac app, linked to your phone. zapzero reads your chats from it, read-only.

items.name: Claude Code
items.text: Logged in with your Claude subscription. It triages, drafts replies in your voice and books your calendar. No key, no new account, no extra cost. Rather nothing leaves your Mac? Use a local model on Ollama.

items.name: OpenRouter
items.text: A key unlocks Jev, a much faster and cheaper classifier for triaging thousands of chats (US$ 0.09 for 1,600). Without it, Claude triages everything.

sections.command:
# 1. Download zapzero.app and drag it to Applications
# 2. Settings → Privacy → Full Disk Access → zapzero
# 3. In the panel, "Connect to Claude" copies this:
claude mcp add --scope user --transport http zapzero \
  http://127.0.0.1:8810/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

sections.title: Categories say when.
sections.body: Besides urgent, this week or stale, every chat gets a tag with its own color: client, hiring, family, someone trying to sell you something. Open Clients and see only the clients waiting on you.

steps.title: Reads how you write.
steps.text: After the first scan, the AI reads your messages, your busiest chats and the groups you write in most.

steps.title: Writes who you are.
steps.text: Where you live, work, family, who matters, what's going on. One topic per field, each one editable.

steps.title: You accept or tweak.
steps.text: Triage knows who's who and every draft comes out in your tone. Changed jobs? Edit one line.

steps.title: Learns from what you change.
steps.text: Every draft you fix becomes an example for the next one. Once a week your fixes turn into new rules for your voice, and you keep the ones that make sense.

sections.title: You confirm the time,
sections.incoming: Call this week? Does Thursday 3pm work? marina@okada.studio
sections.toggle: When I reply, create the event in my calendar

steps.title: You confirm a time.
steps.text: zapzero sees your reply agrees to a day and time and offers to create the event. One tap (or C) turns it on or off.

steps.title: Your Claude books it.
steps.text: When you press Y, zapzero calls your Claude Code, which already has your calendar connected. It creates the event with a call link. zapzero never sees your calendar.

steps.title: And invites them.
steps.text: If their e-mail is in the chat, it goes on the invite. If not, the draft asks for it. When they answer, "add to invite" shows up.

sections.note: Works with the calendar connector your Claude already uses (Google Calendar on claude.ai, for example). It may only create and update events, and only when you reply.

sections.title: How long do you take to answer?

steps.title: Week by week.
steps.text: Thirteen weeks: how often you answered within 24 h and 7 days, how long you take, who never heard back.

steps.title: Counted the right way.
steps.text: A live back-and-forth counts once. Only a message that arrives after yours and after an hour of silence counts as someone waiting.

steps.title: No AI, no cost.
steps.text: It all comes from the local copy of WhatsApp on your Mac. Saved contacts, strangers and groups apart.

items.q: Is it safe for my number?
items.a: Yes. zapzero doesn't connect to WhatsApp: it reads, read-only, the database the official app already keeps on your Mac. No bot, no extra device, no unofficial API, which is what usually gets numbers banned. To WhatsApp, it's just you using the app.

items.q: Does it send messages by itself?
items.a: Never. It opens the chat with the text typed in and stops there. You hit Enter. And anything that's a commitment (a date, an amount, yes or no) comes as a choice for you to decide.

items.q: How do I use it with Claude?
items.a: The app runs a local MCP at 127.0.0.1:8810/mcp, on your Mac only. In the panel's footer, "Connect to Claude" copies the command that adds zapzero to Claude Code. Then just ask: "who's waiting on me?", "what can I archive?". Claude reads and helps you sort. Replying is still you, in WhatsApp.

items.q: Does it work on Windows? On iPhone?
items.a: Not yet. For now it's Mac only, with WhatsApp Desktop installed. The panel opens in any browser on your private network (Tailscale), phone included, but the Mac is what reads the chats.
No one at zapzero: we have no server with your chats. Each chat's excerpt goes only to your Claude (and to Jev, if you turn on OpenRouter).
Nothing extra: zapzero uses the Claude Code on your machine and your Claude subscription. Optional: an OpenRouter key unlocks Jev for faster triage, US$ 0.09 per 1,600 chats.

items.q: macOS says it couldn't verify the app.
items.a: The app isn't signed by Apple yet. Open it once, then go to Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway". All the code is on GitHub, and you can build it yourself with bun run desktop.
